chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Al-Nadr, from one of his companions, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The one who marries a woman intending her wealth, Allah will make that wealth his reliance.'

key_terms.الْجَأَهُ: He made him rely / turn to

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of marrying for wealth according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the Shia emphasis on *ikhlas* (sincerity) in marital unions, warning that marrying for wealth invites divine attachment to that very wealth, potentially leading to spiritual neglect. Scholars interpret this as a caution against materialism corrupting the sacred bond of marriage, contrasting it with the ideal of marrying for religious compatibility and character.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad Bin Bundar, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from his father, from Ahmad Bin Al Nazar, from one of his companions, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The one who marries a woman intending her wealth, Allah<sup>azwj</sup> will Make that wealth his (only) reliance (he loses Faith as reliance has to be upon Allah<sup>azwj</sup>)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bandar has narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from his father from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr from certain persons of his people from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following:
“I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘If one marries a woman for the sake of her wealth, Allah makes that wealth his (only) refuge.’”
